newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon sees no opposition to Hughes.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon sees no opposition to Hughes.

text.p: Raytheon Co said Friday that senior Pentagon officials have voiced no opposition to its proposed takeover of Hughes Electronics Corp's defense business despite a news report otherwise.
In daily deliberations with the Pentagon officials who weigh proposed mergers in the defense industry, Raytheon has not heard any opposition, spokesman Robert McWade said.
"We have had no indications of concerns or problems expressed to us by senior Pentagon officials," he said.
The Wall Street Journal, quoting unnamed Pentagon officials, reported Friday that the Defense Department may seek major changes to the proposed acquisition of the General Motors Corp unit.

The newspaper reported that the Justice Department last week made a sweeping request for new information on the proposed $9.5 billion deal. The Journal said such a formal step often signals anti-trust concerns.
McWade said the department made the request "a while back," and such requests are not at all unusual.
Under a 1994 agreement, defense-company mergers are reviewed by the Justice Department, the Federal Trade Commission and the Pentagon.

The newspaper reported that the Defense Department is most concerned with the concentration the deal would create in the missile business, especially the electronic brains and sensors used in missiles.

"This Hughes deal is completely consistent with the defense consolidation process," McWade said. "Even after these consolidations, Lockheed Martin (Corp ) remains by far the market leader in tactical missiles and electro-optics."
Paul Nisbet, a defense analyst with JSA Research, said that, at worst, the Pentagon could recommend the divestiture of Raytheon's missile focal array components.
"That wouldn't be a deal-buster at all," he said, adding that the combined Raytheon and Hughes business had sales of a few hundred million dollars.
"Most of these mergers have a few stipulations of sorts," he said. "This wouldn't be any different from others that we have seen."
